mainEntity.name: What are the different levels of drywall finish?

acceptedAnswer.text: There are five common levels of drywall finish, ranging from Level 0 to Level 5. Level 0 means no finishing, typically for temporary construction. Level 1 involves embedding tape in joint compound. Level 2 adds a thin coat over all joints and fasteners. Level 3 includes two coats of compound over joints and fasteners, suitable for textured finishes. Level 4 has three coats over joints and fasteners, providing a smooth surface for flat paints or light textures. Level 5 is the highest, with a skim coat over the entire surface, ideal for gloss paints and critical lighting conditions.
acceptedAnswer.description: Drywall finishes range from Level 0 (no finish) to Level 5 (a skim coat over the entire surface). Higher levels provide smoother, more refined walls for different paint types and lighting.
